verdicts.quote: An import is **all-or-nothing**: if any row or file problem exists, no user is created and every problem found is reported.
`rejected`: `created_count` 0 and either one `file_error` (with `line` for `MALFORMED_CSV`) or `errors[]` with `errors_total`; **at most 100 errors are listed** (default), in row order
same normalised email as an earlier row → `EMAIL_DUPLICATE_IN_FILE` with `first_row` ...; else already belongs to an existing user → `EMAIL_EXISTS`.
Imported users get the product's **default non-admin role**; the import can never create an admin.
The import operation succeeds only for a signed-in user who is an admin **at the time of the request**.
verdicts.missing: Whether the import permission is distinct from (not implied by) the permission to create a single user is not stated.

verdicts.quote: A header with only one required column, a duplicated column, or any extra column (e.g. `role`) → `HEADER_INVALID`. A file with no records at all → `HEADER_INVALID`.
valid UTF-8, an optional leading byte-order mark is removed ... records end in LF or CRLF; a field may be quoted with `"`, in which case it may contain commas, line breaks and doubled quotes
every data row becomes a new user in **one atomic commit**: afterwards either all N users exist or none does.
A file larger than **2,097,152 bytes** is rejected `TOO_LARGE`; a file with more than **5,000 data rows** is rejected `TOO_MANY_ROWS`.
A file with no records at all → `HEADER_INVALID`. Header only → `NO_ROWS`. [R-5: One row (N = 1) and 5,000 rows (N = max) behave identically.]
when root uploads V1 again → `rejected`, errors ... `EMAIL_EXISTS` ...; users stay 6 (idempotent re-upload).
The import is **one synchronous request/response**; the response is sent only after the outcome is final. ... At ≤ 5,000 rows no queue is needed
The import sets **no credentials and sends no email**.
How imported users obtain a way to sign in (activation, reset, invitation) is not specified; PD-5 defers it.
verdicts.missing: Whether created users are active or pending and how they first sign in is left undecided.

verdicts.quote: The uploaded bytes and parsed rows live only in the request's memory ... discarded when the response is sent; they are never written to durable storage

For **every** import attempt, including denied ones, exactly one structured log entry is written with: timestamp, actor id (or `anonymous`), outcome, file error code if any, data rows parsed, created count
file or row problems → `rejected`, nothing created; screen Rejected; the admin fixes the file and starts F-1 again.
verdicts.missing: Whether a running import can be cancelled is not stated; retry is only whole-file re-upload.

verdicts.quote: **No numeric latency bound is set here (unresolved):** the only hard bound is the host's request timeout, which is unknown (G-5).
verdicts.missing: A time bound for a maximum-size file; progress is only indeterminate (R-7), not visible progress through the rows.

verdicts.quote: Import is **create-only**: a row whose email already belongs to a user is a row error; existing users are never modified.
verdicts.missing: That the existing single-user creation path keeps working unchanged is not stated.

verdicts.quote: A created user name that begins with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` is stored verbatim; neutralising such values is the duty of any future CSV/spreadsheet export, which this request does not include
